findings.title: Migration 011 breaks existing raw-SQL inserts and shared seed helpers
findings.description: Task 2.1 (task file lines 108-116) adds `BEFORE INSERT` triggers that abort when `owner_id` is null, and the `sessions.machine_id` trigger. Task 3.2 (lines 132-134) only says to bind owner/machine on the 16 production insert statements; it does not update the many existing raw inserts or seeding helpers that execute those same SQL constants. The plan’s own fixture seeding in task 15.1 (line 390) still uses `tests/store/seed.py`, whose existing calls at `tests/store/seed.py:24` and following pass the old parameter count. Raw inserts that will now fail include `tests/store/test_member_removal.py:171`, `tests/store/test_settled.py:84`, `tests/operations/test_pause_held.py:210`, `tests/mcp_server/test_inbox_watcher.py:207`, `tests/live/waking/test_waking_live.py:193`, and the migration tests that call unpatched `migrate(connection)` then insert old-shape rows (for example `tests/store/test_migration_006.py:100`). This leaves the required “full suite at baseline” in design lines 655 and 664 unmet unless every raw insert and helper is updated to bind an acting owner, and sessions to bind `local`.

findings.title: New tables and columns invalidate existing schema and contract pins
findings.description: Task 2.1 (task file lines 108-116) adds four tables, `owner_id` on twelve tables, `sessions.machine_id`, and triggers; task 2.1 line 115 explicitly allows only version-number assertion changes, and context line 55 says no other existing assertion changes. But `tests/test_contract_docs.py:101` pins `len(schema) == 14`; after design lines 403-407 the fresh ordinary table count is 18. `tests/store/test_schema.py:86` compares against a 14-name `TABLES` set. `tests/store/test_schema_holds_no_mirrored_state.py:23` and its doc-parity test pin every `table.column` under fixed reasons, so the new four tables and every new `owner_id`/`machine_id` column break both the pin test and `docs/store-contract.md`’s “Why each column exists” section. No task updates these tests or their documentation parity; task 17.1 saying `tests/test_contract_docs.py` passes is not a step that updates those assertions.

findings.title: Task 3.4’s mechanical replacement is not completable as written
findings.description: Task 3.4 (task file lines 139-140) defines `open_local_store(path)` with a single positional argument and tells a junior AI to replace `Store.open(` everywhere. Existing calls pass `busy_timeout_seconds=SHORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` at `tests/store/test_store.py:91` and `:97`; `tests/operations/test_question_sweep.py:266` and `tests/operations/test_status_sweep.py:48` do the same with short timeouts. Those calls become `TypeError`s unless `open_local_store` forwards the keyword. The same grep also matches `tests/test_store_opened_only_by_state_move.py`, whose docstring and self-test string deliberately contain `Store.open` (`tests/test_store_opened_only_by_state_move.py:1`, `:34`, `:43`); the only named exception is `tests/store/test_schema_holds_no_mirrored_state.py`. Changing that self-test string will break the scan test. Task 3.4 should be split into a helper that preserves all `Store.open` arguments plus a controlled replacement that excludes string-literal fixtures.

findings.title: `StateLayout.client_file` breaks all manual `StateLayout` constructors
findings.description: Task 6.1 (task file line 190) adds `StateLayout.client_file`, but no task updates the six-argument constructors in tests. The existing frozen dataclass has six required fields (`src/amoeba/config/home.py:126-136`), and manual constructions are at `tests/mcp_server/test_detached.py:219`, `tests/operations/state_move_support.py:41`, `tests/operations/state_move_worker.py:36`, `tests/operations/test_prune.py:55`, and `tests/operations/test_prune_wiring.py:75`. Adding a required field makes those helpers fail at runtime, and pyright will fail too. The plan’s task 6.1 success criterion only mentions `tests/config`; it does not cover these dependent callers.

findings.title: New CLI-only commands have no `cli.main` dispatch path in the tasks
findings.description: Tasks 13.4 and 14.2 (task file lines 357-359 and 372-375) add `join`, `leave`, and five `hub ...` commands as CLI-only commands with no `OperationName`. The existing `main()` only dispatches the `cli_only` value `WAKE_RUN_COMMAND` (`src/amoeba/cli/main.py:50-55`); any other command with no `operation` reaches `if name is None: raise AssertionError(...)`. Task 14.3 line 377 changes `cli/main.py` only for `handle-pause` and `wake-run` entry-point checks. No task says to update the runner dispatch for the new CLI-only commands or to extend `CLI_ONLY_COMMANDS`. As written, `amoeba hub --help`/`amoeba join --help` success criteria can pass while actual commands fail before `hub_commands.py` or `join_command.py` is reached.

findings.title: A join killed after writing the closed mark but before renaming has no undo command
findings.description: Task 4.2 (task file lines 156-158) makes every write transaction, including `call_scope`, reject a store once `closed_mark` has a row. Task 13.2 (lines 348-350) defines `set_aside` as “write the closed mark, checkpoint, rename” and only gives idempotent skipping to `put_back`; task 13.5 line 362 tests the state after the rename, not the kill between the closed mark and the rename. If `join --set-aside-local` is killed after writing the mark but before renaming, the store is still at the store path with a closed mark, no client file, and no set-aside file. A re-run cannot use `store.write()` because the new closed-mark guard rolls it back; `leave()` looks only for a set-aside file to clear and rename (task 13.2 line 349), so it cannot clear the mark at the store path either. Design D4 lines 225-229 require killed join/leave states to be finishable; this state is only endable by editing files.

findings.title: Docker-unavailable state can reach final validation with required design notes incomplete
findings.description: Task 16.2 (task file lines 419-421) says that when Docker is unavailable, write `BLOCKED` and stop; it then says 17.3 waits while 17.1, 17.2, and 17.4 go on. Task 17.3 line 435 requires the Implementation Notes entry to include the container output summary from 16.2; task 17.4 lines 437-442 still declares final validation success and has the final `**Commit**:` at line 444. There is no later command that resumes 17.3, records a Docker-blocked substitute, or prevents final validation/commit while 17.3 is incomplete. This violates the sequence rule that every state a step can leave must be continued or undone, and it leaves design D19 line 553’s slice-notes requirement unmet.

findings.title: `open_hub_store` is not explicitly placed in `state_move.py`
findings.description: Task 3.3 (task file line 136) says `state_move.py` stays the only caller of `Store.open`, matching design D12 lines 414-417 and the existing AST test at `tests/test_store_opened_only_by_state_move.py:29-40`, which scans every source module except `operations/state_move.py`. Task 6.3 line 201 adds `open_hub_store(layout)` that calls `Store.open`, but it never names the module. A junior AI can place this helper anywhere; if it lands in a new `hub/store_open.py` or other module, the AST test fails. State explicitly that `open_hub_store` is added to `operations/state_move.py` or update the AST test and design D12’s “only caller” invariant.

findings.title: Moving the five operational error classes would break existing imports and pins
findings.description: Task 10.1a (task file line 278) says to “move today’s five operational error types” into `operations/errors.py`. The current classes live elsewhere: `AmoebaHomeError` at `src/amoeba/config/home.py:41`, `ConfigError` at `src/amoeba/config/user_config.py:44`, `ContextForgeError` at `src/amoeba/operations/members.py:24`, `SquadronError` at `src/amoeba/upstream/squadron/errors.py:6`, and `StoreError` at `src/amoeba/store/errors.py:10`. Many source and test modules import those original names; `tests/test_wiring.py:101` pins `wiring.OPERATIONAL_ERRORS` to those classes. If the definitions actually move, those imports and the test pin break; if only a tuple is moved/re-exported, the task wording is wrong. The task should specify defining `OPERATION_ERRORS` from the existing classes plus compatibility re-exports, or list every import update.

findings.title: The `decisions` and `standing` signature changes do not enumerate all production and test callers
findings.description: Tasks 7.1 and 7.2 (task file lines 212-217) change `decisions(store, document, *, deps)` and `standing(..., run=...)` to new readers/resolvers; task 7.4 line 225 says `wiring._dispatch` sends six cases through `run_served`, but no task retires `wiring_standing.place_standing`, whose signature at `src/amoeba/wiring_standing.py:27` still calls old `standing`. Any leftover import of `place_standing` in `wiring.py` also fails ruff. Existing calls extend beyond “its tests”: `tests/operations/test_mark_read.py:146`, `tests/operations/test_retract.py:58`, `tests/operations/test_prune.py:249`, `tests/operations/test_list_standing.py:39`, `tests/operations/test_withdraw.py:31`, and many modules found by the search. Context line 55 mentions “call sites in 7.1 and 7.2,” but the tasks do not give a complete caller list or say to update test helper rigs that build old `Deps`/`CfRun` fakes.

findings.title: Wheel inclusion of `hub.yaml.example` is not actually tested
findings.description: Task 8.1 (task file line 242) adds `src/amoeba/hub/hub.yaml.example` to wheel artifacts, and line 244 says `tests/test_wheel_contents.py` passes “with the example listed in it.” The existing root wheel test only asserts the baseline migration and entry point; there is no assertion for the new artifact, and there is no task that changes this test. Design D17 lines 519-520 requires the example to come from the wheel and says “A test loads `hub.yaml.example` as a valid hub config.” Task 8.4’s config validity test can use the source file, while task 16.1 line 415 copies from `/usr/share/amoeba/`. Add a wheel-content assertion and a container/wheel path check, or the container can silently ship a missing example.

findings.title: “Client file with no saved certificate fails every call” is under-tested
findings.description: Design Functional Requirement line 634 says a client file with no saved certificate fails every call with `ClientFileError` naming the file, and `leave` still works. Task 6.4 line 204 tests `load_client_file` and `read_client_address`; task 13.5 line 362 tests only “a client file with no certificate fails a served call” and `leave`; task 14.4 line 382 uses a home with a saved certificate. No task covers `handle-pause`, `wake-run`, unserved MCP tools, or `answer` with a missing certificate, even though `mcp/in_process.py:53` currently performs an `answer` deadline/config check before `wiring.invoke`. Without a test that all entry points call `joined()` first and create no files, design D2 line 157 and FR line 634 are not fully proven.

findings.title: Integration requirement for 261 extensibility has no corresponding task or test
findings.description: Design Integration Requirement line 663 says “261 can serve a new operation by adding to the served list and `run_served`, with no change to the call format.” Tasks 1.2, 7.3, 10.1b, and 12.3 build the current protocol, but no task asserts or maps this extensibility requirement. Task 17.4 line 439 maps only “each Functional Requirement,” not Integration Requirements. The gap leaves the named integration criterion unproven; add a small test that a new served name can be passed through the unchanged request/reply shapes without changing `client.call` or `handle_call`, or explicitly map the requirement to the existing contract tests.

findings.title: Load NFR has a `tests/load` task and explicit CI gating
findings.description: The design restates load bounds in D18 line 532, D14 line 478, and Technical Requirement line 657. Task 15.6 (task file lines 405-408) adds `tests/load/test_door_load.py` with both bounds and records measured figures. The same task explicitly names the `Tests` step of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, confirms that `pyproject.toml` only ignores `tests/live`, and requires `pytest --collect-only` for the new file. CI gating is therefore explicit rather than implicit; no CI edit is needed with the existing bare `uv run pytest` gate.

findings.title: Task file is overweight in a few local areas
findings.description: The single file has 17 sections, 70 numbered tasks, and 443 lines. Most of the size is justified by the slice, but some tasks are too large/underspecified to be independently completable: task 3.4 spans 114 files plus helper signatures and AST self-tests; task 13.5 bundles join, set-aside, leave, interrupted-step, and missing-certificate tests; task 15.1 bundles subprocess lifecycle, real CLI invite/join, seeding, and client runners. Split 3.4 into “helper with full `Store.open` signature” + “controlled replacement” + “full-suite repair”; split 13.5 into normal join/leave, set-aside/leave recovery, and interrupted-step tests; merge or cut the repeated administrative notes in 0.1, 0.2, 17.3, and 17.4 that restate branch/baseline/mapping bookkeeping. This reduces over-broad edits while keeping the design’s required test coverage.
